summary_hint: Flood policy <policy_number> from <insurance_carrier_or_nfip_wyo_company> on <insured_property_address>, <effective_date>-<expiration_date>, building coverage <building_coverage_limit> / deductible <building_deductible>, status <policy_status>, premium <premium_paid_status> — the adequacy inputs IH-6 checks against the SFHA zone

typed_core.name: insurance_carrier_or_nfip_wyo_company
typed_core.why: IH-6 — the policy's source; NFIP vs WYO vs private governs the adequacy standard

typed_core.name: named_insureds
typed_core.why: IH-6 — must include the borrower; flattened person_or_entity[] -> primary + _2

typed_core.name: insured_property_address
typed_core.why: IH-6 — must match the subject property the SFHA determination covers

typed_core.name: policy_number
typed_core.why: PII (restricted) — policy identity; promote so it is masked, not left unmasked in the catch-all

typed_core.name: policy_form_or_program
typed_core.why: disambiguator — NFIP Dwelling Form vs General Property vs private 'equivalent'; the form sets what 'adequate' means

typed_core.name: effective_date
typed_core.why: IH-6 — policy must be in force at/through closing

typed_core.name: expiration_date
typed_core.why: IH-6 — must remain valid through closing

typed_core.name: flood_zone
typed_core.why: IH-6 disambiguator — the SFHA trigger; the dec page often restates the zone so it can be cross-checked against the flood determination
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture the restated flood zone to cross-check the determination; surface conflicts rather than trusting one source

typed_core.name: community_and_map_information
typed_core.why: disambiguator for flood_zone — NFIP community/panel that anchors the zone

typed_core.name: building_coverage_limit
typed_core.why: IH-6 — the primary adequacy input (compared to loan balance / replacement cost / NFIP max)
typed_core.prompt_hint: Distinguish the dwelling/building coverage from contents coverage; the building limit is the IH-6 input

typed_core.name: building_deductible
typed_core.why: IH-6 — an excessive deductible can make coverage inadequate

typed_core.name: replacement_cost_or_actual_cash_value_basis
typed_core.why: IH-6 disambiguator — RCV vs ACV changes whether the limit is adequate (the IH-1 settlement-basis lesson: the same word can mean the dwelling or contents row)
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture the row it belongs to (the dwelling/building basis); don't grab the first 'replacement cost' on the page

typed_core.name: premium_paid_status
typed_core.why: IH-6 — coverage is only in force if the (first) premium is paid

typed_core.name: waiting_period_or_effective_condition
typed_core.why: IH-6 — the NFIP 30-day waiting period vs the closing date determines whether the policy is actually effective at closing

typed_core.name: lender_loan_number
typed_core.why: identity/linkage — ties the policy to the loan file (confidential)

nested_lists.name: mortgagee_clause_entries
nested_lists.shape_reason: a policy lists 1-3 mortgagees/loss-payees (lender, servicer, trustee) — few items, so a flat row is light

fields.name: mortgagee_name
fields.why: IH-6 — the lender must be named as mortgagee; warrantability

fields.name: loan_number
fields.why: IH-6 — ties the mortgagee entry to the loan file

fields.name: source
fields.why: provenance — where on the dec page this entry was read

rejected.name: document_title, form_number, form_revision_date
rejected.reason: classification/version before extraction (policy_form_or_program identifies the program)

rejected.name: document_issue_date, declarations_or_endorsement_date
rejected.reason: issue/endorsement dates are marginal beside effective/expiration; catch-all

rejected.name: statement_period_start/_end
rejected.reason: the policy term is effective/expiration, not a statement period

rejected.name: party_names, party_addresses
rejected.reason: covered by named_insureds + insured_property_address + the mortgagee list

rejected.name: signature_blocks, notary_block
rejected.reason: a dec page is issued by the carrier, not executed/notarized; catch-all

rejected.name: basement_or_other_limitations
rejected.reason: coverage nuance; marginal for IH-6 adequacy; catch-all

rejected.name: agent_or_producer_contact
rejected.reason: producer contact; no IH-6 gate; catch-all

encoding_variations: flood_zone — SFHA set A/AE/AO/AH/AR/A99, V/VE vs non-SFHA X/B/C/D. The authoritative zone is on the flood determination; the policy dec page restates it and can lag — capture it as a cross-check, flag conflicts

replacement_cost_or_actual_cash_value_basis — 'Replacement Cost', 'RCV', 'ACV', 'Actual Cash Value'. No enum coercer; the dwelling basis can sit beside a different contents basis — capture the row it belongs to, don't grab the first 'replacement cost' on the page
policy_status / premium_paid_status — 'Active/In Force', 'Cancelled', 'Expired', 'Pending' and 'Paid', 'Paid in Full', 'Balance Due', 'Not Paid'. No enum coercer; degrade to str
insurance_carrier_or_nfip_wyo_company — NFIP Direct vs a WYO (Write-Your-Own) carrier issuing NFIP policies vs a private flood carrier; the program governs adequacy
waiting_period — usually 30 days for new NFIP purchases (waived on loan closing); capture the stated condition

open_questions.q: BLOCKED status — IH-6 has no producer yet. Should the schema land the adequacy fields now so the rule lights up when unblocked, rather than the values reaching the discarded catch-all?
options: wait until IH-6 has a producer

open_questions.q: RCV/ACV basis disambiguation — the biggest misread risk: the dwelling basis vs the contents basis
options: one replacement_cost_or_actual_cash_value_basis str + a prompt hint to read the dwelling row
split into building_ and contents_ basis fields

open_questions.q: Zone-source conflict — the policy's restated zone may disagree with the flood determination (the authoritative source)
open_questions.recommendation: capture both; IH-6 keys on the determination; surface conflicts for review

open_questions.q: Adequacy threshold owner — the 'adequate' comparison (limit vs lesser of loan/replacement/NFIP max) is a rule computation, not an extracted fact
open_questions.recommendation: confirm the schema only lands the inputs and leaves the adequacy judgment to IH-6

notes: No existing_extractor for this document type — new schema.
IH-6 status is BLOCKED (no producer yet); the fields must still land now so IH-6 activates when unblocked rather than the values going to the discarded catch-all.
19 typed-core rows + one nested list. IH-6 keys on presence (policy_number/dates/status), adequacy (building limit/deductible/basis), the SFHA zone, and the mortgagee clause. Within range.

This is a flood policy / declarations page (NFIP Dwelling Form, WYO, or private-flood equivalent), not the flood determination — the determination gives the SFHA zone; the policy gives coverage. Distinguish the dwelling/building coverage from contents coverage; the building limit is the IH-6 input. Money with $/commas -> Decimal; mask the policy number.

PII: policy_number needs _PII_FIELDS registration, pre_masked false (restricted; otherwise stored unmasked in the catch-all). named_insureds are person/entity names at standard sensitivity (identity). insured_property_address is the subject collateral, not restricted borrower PII. lender_loan_number is confidential but a loan identifier, not a maskable PII kind.
